rv.q: Lighter than air and grounded in ache, it’s the emotional peak of the show, and very possibly of this fall season.
It’s a sure cure for any lingering Weltschmerz.
Few musicals from the era are as airtight, inventive, or downright lovable.
Off Broadway at New World Stages, all the elements have stacked up splendidly in a revival of the show that arrives 20 years after the Broadway premiere and captures every drop of the original charm.

Once again, we are witnessing a moment of perfect syzygy with the revival of Rachel Sheinkin and William Finn's musical now playing at New World Stages, and it is as delightful and effervescent as ever.

The great irony of this revival of Spelling Bee is that the exemplary performances that make this a must-see production are almost certainly the product of the same merciless meritocracy that places children in competition at an early age.

A full-hearted, belly-laughing confection from the early 2000s, this new production of Spelling Bee swoops in like a big hug from an old friend, reminding us of everything we fell in love with two decades ago.
He sees the material with fresh eyes and delivers a sparkling, warm, and intimate production.
For 105 minutes, this delightfully wise and witty musical is the ideal antidote for anyone needing a return of innocence and laughter in their upended lives.
Twenty years later, this charming Off-Broadway revival proves Spelling Bee‘s blend of silly wordplay and surprising heart remains unbeatable.
Spelling Bee is the perfect antidote to these dreary anxiety-ridden times, and it’s worth settling down for a long, laughter-induced spell.
The Off-Broadway revival of The 25th Annual Putnam County Spelling Bee, choreographed and directed by Danny Mefford, is pretty close to letter-perfect.
This production understands the delicate balance of comedy and sincerity that makes Spelling Bee work, and it nails it.

cn.t: Critics hail this 20th-anniversary revival as joyous, warm, and letter-perfect, with Finn and Sheinkin's musical proving as delightful and emotionally resonant as ever. The cast earns universal praise in a production deemed a perfect salve for difficult times.

vr.q: This is one of my biggest New York musical theater recommendations right now. I can't wait to go back to the show. I thought it was a delight.
i really couldn't have asked for a better way to revisit the show after all these years and especially if you're not yet familiar with the show i really think this is a must see
What a fantastic show still and this new cast is incredible. Nina White had me freaking bawling at the I love you song.
Overall, the bee is a must-see.
This is a very good production of a show that I love... It has earned its extended run and then some.
